name: architecture-workshop-facilitation-suite
known_facts: No workshop should run longer than 4 hours without a break
More than 10 participants should break into working groups
Start every session by restating the outcome

input.workshop_title: AWS to Azure Migration — Architecture Decision Workshop
input.stakeholders: Cloud Architect, Security Lead, Platform Engineering Lead, Product Manager, Network Engineer
input.desired_outcome: Agreed migration strategy with workload prioritization and timeline
input.pre_read_materials: Current AWS architecture diagrams, migration cost analysis, Azure Landing Zone documentation
input.objective_2: Identified networking and security dependencies between workloads
input.objective_3: Draft migration timeline with go/no-go decision points
input.contribution_1: Technical feasibility of each migration wave
input.bias_1: May prefer keeping some workloads on AWS due to technical debt
input.contribution_2: Compliance requirements and security controls for Azure Landing Zone
input.bias_2: May default to most restrictive option rather than risk-based
input.contribution_3: Operational readiness and CI/CD pipeline changes required
input.bias_3: May underestimate migration complexity for legacy workloads
input.pre_work_description: Review current AWS architecture diagrams and complete workload assessment spreadsheet by workshop date
input.activity_1: Opening — restate outcome, review ground rules, round-robin introductions
input.note_1: Keep introductions to 2 min each. Write ground rules on board. Confirm desired outcome is still correct.
input.output_1: Confirmed workshop objectives and ground rules
input.activity_2: Workload prioritization — review assessment scores, agree top 10
input.note_2: Use dot voting for workload priority. Flag any workload that appears in every team's top 10.
input.note_3: Strongly encourage people to step away from screens
input.activity_4: Dependency mapping — network, security, data dependencies between top 10 workloads
input.note_4: Draw dependency graph on Miro. Highlight cycles and critical path.
input.output_4: Dependency graph with identified critical path
input.activity_5: Close — review decisions, assign owners, schedule follow-up
input.note_5: Decisions made > open items > risks. Explicit check: does everyone agree with the path forward?
input.output_5: Decision log with owners and follow-up schedule
input.criterion_assessment_1: Number of dependencies, data volume, and refactoring required
input.criterion_assessment_2: Revenue impact, user count, and regulatory implications of downtime
input.criterion_assessment_3: Data sensitivity, compliance boundary change, and blast radius
input.constraint_1: Azure Landing Zone must be compliant before any workload migration
input.constraint_2: No workload can have more than 4 hours of planned downtime
input.constraint_3: Active Directory synchronization must be completed before application migration
input.rationale_1: Lowest dependency count and highest business impact — quick wins build momentum
input.impact_1: If wave 1 migrates slower than planned, wave 2-4 timeline compresses
input.decision_2: Azure Landing Zone will use Azure Lighthouse for delegated management
input.rationale_2: Simplest path to compliance separation without duplicating management tooling
input.impact_2: Lighthouse delegation model may need adjustment for DoD workloads
input.open_item_1: Confirm Azure Lighthouse scope with compliance team
input.open_item_2: Network throughput validation between region pairs
input.risk_1: Legacy .NET Framework 4.8 apps may not run on Azure App Service Linux
input.mitigation_1: Identify Windows App Service or container-based alternative before wave 2
input.risk_2: Data sync latency between Azure regions may exceed SLA for the search workload
input.mitigation_2: Evaluate Azure Front Door and Cosmos DB multi-region writes
